title: Ezekiel 48:23–29
context: The Lord GOD lists the tribes south of the holy portion: Benjamin, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, and Gad, each receiving “one portion,” and the southern border runs from Tamar to the waters of Meribath Kadesh, to the brook, and to the great sea, closing with “This is the land which you shall divide by lot to the tribes of Israel for inheritance.”

verses.text: “As for the rest of the tribes: from the east side to the west side, Benjamin, one portion.
verses.arminianNotes:
“As for the rest of the tribes: from the east side to the west side, Benjamin, one portion.” Arminian readers note that Benjamin lies just south of the holy portion.

Judah and Benjamin now border the center on either side.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise note Benjamin’s place near the sanctuary and hold explanations lightly.

Shared ground: both traditions read the verse as continuing the orderly division of the land.

verses.text: “By the border of Benjamin, from the east side to the west side, Simeon, one portion.
verses.arminianNotes:
“By the border of Benjamin, from the east side to the west side, Simeon, one portion.” Arminian readers note that Simeon receives its own portion.

In Joshua 19:1, Simeon’s inheritance lay within Judah.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise note the difference from the earlier allotment without harmonizing it.

Shared ground: both traditions read the verse as part of the equal division promised in 47:14.

verses.text: “By the border of Simeon, from the east side to the west side, Issachar, one portion.
verses.arminianNotes:
“By the border of Simeon, from the east side to the west side, Issachar, one portion.” Arminian readers note that Issachar, once in the north, is placed in the south.

The new map differs from the old.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise note the change and hold any explanation lightly.

Shared ground: both traditions agree that the text does not explain the rearrangement and read the verse as part of the orderly list.

verses.text: “By the border of Issachar, from the east side to the west side, Zebulun, one portion.
verses.arminianNotes:
“By the border of Issachar, from the east side to the west side, Zebulun, one portion.” Arminian readers note that Zebulun is also moved south.

The pattern of equal strips continues.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see the list proceeding in order.

Shared ground: both traditions read the verse simply as part of the tribal allotments, without symbolic pressure on Zebulun’s position.

verses.text: “By the border of Zebulun, from the east side to the west side, Gad, one portion.
verses.arminianNotes:
“By the border of Zebulun, from the east side to the west side, Gad, one portion.” Arminian readers note that Gad, once east of the Jordan, now lies at the southern edge.

Gad, like Dan, Asher, and Naphtali, descends from a servant wife (Gen 30).
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise hold observations about the order lightly.

Shared ground: both traditions agree that the text gives no reason for Gad’s position, and read the verse as completing the southern tribes.

verses.text: “By the border of Gad, at the south side southward, the border shall be even from Tamar to the waters of Meribath Kadesh, to the brook, to the great sea.
verses.arminianNotes:
The southern edge is given: “the border shall be even from Tamar to the waters of Meribath Kadesh, to the brook, to the great sea.” Arminian readers note that the southern border repeats 47:19.

The land’s limits are restated.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see the boundary confirmed.

Shared ground: both traditions hold the place identifications with care and read the verse as closing the description of the southern edge.

verses.text: “This is the land which you shall divide by lot to the tribes of Israel for inheritance, and these are their several portions, says the Lord GOD.
verses.arminianNotes:
“This is the land which you shall divide by lot to the tribes of Israel for inheritance,” says the Lord GOD. Arminian readers note the summary of the division.

The lot recalls the earlier division under Joshua.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see the inheritance granted by God’s word.

Shared ground: both traditions agree that the land is a gift from the LORD, divided according to his promise.
